Bermuda Banking Sector Faces Credit Freeze Amid Liquidity Crunch

HAMILTON, Bermuda — The Bermudian banking industry is grappling with a severe credit freeze following a sudden liquidity crisis that began late last week, industry representatives said Tuesday. The disruption has prompted several major banks to halt new lending, while smaller firms warn of possible site closures and job cuts if the situation persists.

The crisis unfolded after a sharp decline in offshore capital inflows, which local analysts attribute to heightened global risk aversion and a series of large loan defaults reported by the industry. As a result, banks such as Hamilton National and Coral Bank have suspended new loan approvals and limited client withdrawals, citing the need to preserve liquidity.

“The sector is experiencing unprecedented stress,” said Michael Dill, president of the Bermuda Banking Association. “Our members are working closely with regulators to stabilize operations, but the immediate priority is safeguarding customer deposits and maintaining essential services.”

Employees in the sector are reporting growing uncertainty. “Staff have been told that branch hours may be reduced, and there is a freeze on overtime,” said a spokesperson for the Bermuda Bank Workers Union. “We are seeking assurances that jobs will be protected, but the outlook is unclear.”

At several banking offices in Hamilton, workers were seen leaving early as some sites closed temporarily. According to industry sources, at least three mid-sized banks are considering consolidating branches or reducing workforce numbers if the liquidity crunch continues through the next quarter.

Regulators have called for emergency talks with bank executives to coordinate a response, but as of Tuesday afternoon, no industry-wide recovery plan had been announced. “The situation is extremely fluid,” said Dill. “We are monitoring developments hour by hour.”
